name: Bronco Test
summary: A maximal-effort conditioning shuttle test consisting of five continuous rounds of 20-meter, 40-meter, and 60-meter out-and-back sprints totaling 1,200 meters.

setup: Set out cones along a straight running lane at 0 meters (start line), 20 meters, 40 meters, and 60 meters.
Take an athletic two-point stance directly behind the 0-meter starting line.
steps: Sprint forward to the 20-meter line, touch or cross the line, and sprint back to the 0-meter line.
Immediately turn and sprint forward to the 40-meter line, touch or cross the line, and sprint back to the 0-meter line.
Immediately turn and sprint forward to the 60-meter line, touch or cross the line, and sprint back across the 0-meter line to complete one round (240 meters).
Without pausing, repeat this entire shuttle sequence four more times for a total of five rounds (1,200 meters total).
Stop the timer the moment you cross the 0-meter line at the end of the fifth 60-meter return sprint.
instructions.breathing: Maintain controlled, rhythmic deep breathing throughout the test, focusing on steady exhalations during turns.
cues: Drop your center of gravity to decelerate into each turn.
Drive hard out of the turn with short, powerful strides.
Alternate your turning lead leg to distribute fatigue evenly.

common_faults.fault: Cutting turns short before touching or crossing the marker line.
common_faults.correction: Ensure your lead foot touches or clearly crosses the cone line on every single turn.

common_faults.fault: Sprinting the first round at maximum effort and suffering severe premature exhaustion.
common_faults.correction: Pace the opening round at a controlled, high-threshold tempo rather than an all-out sprint to keep lap splits consistent.

common_faults.fault: Always turning off the same leg, overloading one side and slowing directional changes.
common_faults.correction: Alternate the planting and turning leg between lines to balance fatigue and maintain sharp changes of direction.

precautions: Ensure appropriate footwear with solid traction for the running surface (cleats for grass/turf, running shoes for track) to prevent slipping during rapid directional changes.
Complete a thorough dynamic warm-up including sprint accelerations and decelerations prior to testing.
